newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end unchanged after Summers meeting.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end unchanged after Summers meeting.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures closed steady on Tuesday, after fears that Japan's finance minister would unveil an economic stimulus plan at a meeting with U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers proved groundless, traders said.
Such fears helped trigger large-lot selling of December futures in the morning, but short covering in the afternoon lifted the contract back to an unchanged close at 99.19.
The contract traded from 99.17 to 99.20 on turnover of 57,639 lots.

Summers called on Japan to achieve its official economic growth target of 1.9 percent in 1997/98, led by domestic demand. While Japanese finance minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka said Japan would strive to achieve domestically driven growth, he did not unveil any concrete measures to achieve that goal.
He also assured Summers that there was no need for concern about Japan's financial system, a senior MOF official said in a briefing for reporters on the meeting between Summers and Mitsuzuka.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) carried out an accommodative operation on Tuesday morning for the third day in a row, confirming views it would not lift interest rates anytime soon.
Traders said the accommodative stance was already factored into the market, however, and with no fresh factors to encourage buying, participants were encouraged to test the downside.

"The contract is now in a downtrend toward 99.15," said a city bank dealer. "Whether or not the goverment can set up a plan to stop the decline in land prices will be a focus (for the market), as such a plan would trigger further selling."

The key overnight interbank rate firmed despite the BOJ's accommodative operation, trading mainly at 0.49 percent, up from Monday's 0.48. The rate was underpinned by continued demand from banks for short-term funds ahead of the fiscal year-end on March 31, traders said.
The firmness at the short end also affected longer-term money rates, as fund suppliers were hesitant to lower rates.

Benchmark three-month certificates of deposit (CD) were issued at 0.54 percent, against 0.54 and 0.53 percent on Monday. The issued rate of two-month CDs rose to 0.55 percent from 0.54. -- Risa Maeda Tokyo Treasury +81-33432-8570
